title: Chiasm as an Applied Theory and Methodology for Nature Connectedness: A 30-Day Intervention Enhancing Well-Being and Pro-Environmental Behaviour
content: Reconnecting people with the rest of nature is increasingly identified as a deep leverage point for sustainability, because nature connectedness (NC) predicts pro-environmental behaviour and human well-being simultaneously. Yet the mechanisms through which NC actually changes remain poorly specified, which limits the design of effective interventions, and dominant measures overlook the embodied, perceptual and relational dimensions of everyday connectedness. NC research also rarely makes its own epistemological standpoint explicit, and so risks reproducing the subject–object separation that sustainability transformations seek to unsettle. We address both problems through chiasm—Merleau-Ponty’s conceptualisation of perception as simultaneously active and passive—used as theory and as methodology. We conducted a 30-day quasi-experimental intervention with 55 university students in Shiraz, Iran (27 intervention, 28 control), a non-WEIRD, place-rich context in which culturally transmitted practices of perception such as tamāšā (‘watching while walking’) already carry chiastic qualities. Participants shared daily nature experiences in small mobile messaging groups across five thematic modules (senses, beauty, emotion, meaning, compassion). Nature relatedness, pro-environmental behaviour, psychological well-being and mindfulness were measured on days 0, 15 and 30 as the ‘outside view’; participants’ shared experiences were coded for chiastic structure as the ‘inside view’. Chiastic experiences increased significantly across the intervention, as did nature relatedness, pro-environmental behaviour, well-being and mindfulness relative to controls. Chiasm offers a plausible relational mechanism for NC change and a low-cost, culturally grounded and scalable intervention format that advances human well-being and sustainable behaviour together, contributing to SDGs 3, 12, 13 and 15.
